_why: corpus-map-off-the-request: a read never computes the corpus map. After a setting the map reads (analysis-defaults iou) changes, the home page draws the LAST map at once with a muted 'updating' notice over it (coverage-stale) while a worker process recomputes, re-reads every 3 s, and drops the notice when the fresh map lands. Before, the read recomputed inside the request (~100 s on the post-RQ4 database) and every page stalled behind it. The disk cache keeps ONE file per question, so the recompute for the changed iou overwrites the map of the original setting: putting iou back is a second change and a SECOND full recompute. The state re-reads after the restore and waits that one out too, so it leaves no recompute behind. The waits are 400 s each (a full-fixture recompute took 148-259 s under load); the whole state can take ~15 min on the real database. If iou was never saved before, the restore writes 0.5 explicitly (a settings row now exists).

actions.eval: async () => { const g = await fetch('/api/settings/analysis-defaults').then(r => r.json()); const was = (g.values && typeof g.values.iou === 'number') ? g.values.iou : 0.5; window.__ubSmokeIou = was; try { sessionStorage.setItem('ub-smoke-iou', String(was)) } catch (e) {} const r = await fetch('/api/settings/analysis-defaults', {method: 'PUT', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify({values: {iou: was === 0.49 ? 0.48 : 0.49}, actor: 'smoke corpus-map', previous: {iou: was}})}); if (!r.ok) throw new Error('PUT analysis-defaults iou: ' + r.status + ' ' + await r.text()) }

async () => { let was = window.__ubSmokeIou; if (typeof was !== 'number') { try { was = Number(sessionStorage.getItem('ub-smoke-iou')) } catch (e) {} } if (typeof was !== 'number' || !isFinite(was)) was = 0.5; const r = await fetch('/api/settings/analysis-defaults', {method: 'PUT', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify({values: {iou: was}, actor: 'smoke corpus-map'})}); if (!r.ok) throw new Error('restoring analysis-defaults iou: ' + r.status + ' ' + await r.text()) }
